title: Fast-Moving Consumer Goods
gist: This is a BCG practice-page rollup for its FMCG consulting business, framing five strategic imperatives (portfolio management, demand-model reinvention, digital end-to-end, operating-model agility, purpose) and citing Nestle's CHF 2.5 billion restructuring plus pointers to BCG research on shifting consumer behavior, declining alcohol volumes, expanding beauty demand, and the limits of AI in supply chain planning.

insights.claim: BCG frames FMCG strategy around five imperatives it says are vital for sustained success: continuous portfolio reshaping, reinventing the demand model, building digital end-to-end capabilities, elevating the operating model, and anchoring purpose in company history.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Useful checklist for benchmarking whether a consumer-goods portfolio company is executing against the full transformation agenda BCG is selling to the sector, not just cost-cutting.
insights.quote: Our FMCG consultants work shoulder to shoulder with clients to enable them to meet five strategic imperatives vital for sustaining success.
insights.locator: How BCG Helps the FMCG Sector Meet Five Strategic Imperatives

insights.claim: BCG advises FMCG companies to act as 'always-on portfolio managers,' proactively buying and selling brands/assets and skewing organic investment toward leading brand positions rather than chasing short-term margin gains.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Signals BCG expects continued active M&A and brand-portfolio churn (divestitures of laggard brands, bolt-on acquisitions) across large consumer-goods conglomerates.
insights.quote: Reshape your portfolio further and faster by proactively buying and selling assets to build advantaged positions and skew organic growth investment by emphasizing leading brand positions over short-term margin gains.

insights.claim: BCG's demand-model playbook for FMCG centers on using proprietary technology and 360-degree customer data to personalize marketing down to 'segments of one,' beyond traditional broad demographic segmentation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Points to continued capex/opex shift toward first-party data and personalization tech among consumer-goods majors as a growth lever, relevant for martech and data-platform vendors serving CPG.
insights.quote: engage with consumers on a personal level, such as by combining new technology and 360-degree customer profiles to target “segments of one,”

insights.claim: BCG is pushing FMCG clients to deploy AI at scale across supply chains to improve demand forecasting and efficiency, alongside hyperflexible go-to-market and net revenue management systems.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Consistent with broader enterprise AI adoption in supply chain/forecasting; watch for CPG capex announcements tied to AI-driven demand planning and revenue management platforms.
insights.quote: Bring AI to scale across your supply chain by investing in digital platforms to better forecast demand and turbocharge efficiency.

insights.claim: Nestle undertook a CHF 2.5 billion organizational transformation aimed at boosting efficiency and cutting costs specifically to free up capital to reinvest in innovation and growth.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete benchmark for the scale of restructuring spend large-cap food/consumer companies are undertaking; useful comparator when evaluating peer cost-cutting programs (Unilever, P&G, etc.) for credibility and scale.
insights.quote: Nestlé’s CHF 2.5 Billion Transformation to Boost Efficiency, Cut Costs, and Fuel Growth

insights.claim: BCG characterizes current global consumer behavior change as a 'seismic shift,' identifying five consumer-led themes it says indicate where FMCG growth will emerge next and implying that many companies' existing growth strategies have not kept pace.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A flag that legacy category-growth assumptions in consumer staples may be stale; worth cross-checking against the referenced BCG consumer-themes report before underwriting FMCG growth forecasts.
insights.quote: A seismic shift in consumer behavior is underway. Five consumer-led themes reveal where demand is heading and where the next wave of growth will emerge.
insights.locator: Global Consumers Have Moved On. Has Your Growth Strategy Caught Up?

insights.claim: BCG says the global alcohol market is facing declining sales, and the brands winning share are those tailoring products to the specific occasion, location, and reason consumers choose to drink rather than competing on broad category volume.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Relevant read-through for alcoholic beverage names (spirits, beer, RTDs) facing volume declines: occasion-based product segmentation (low/no-alcohol, ready-to-drink formats) is positioned as the offsetting growth lever.
insights.quote: The alcohol market is confronting declining sales. Brands that win tailor their products to how, where, and why consumers now choose to drink.
insights.locator: Why Owning the Moment Wins in a Changing Alcohol Market

insights.claim: A Women's Wear Daily and BCG survey of 5,000 US beauty consumers found the beauty industry is expanding demand beyond traditional beauty solutions into adjacent categories.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Suggests beauty TAM expansion (e.g., into wellness/health-adjacent products) is a live growth vector worth tracking in beauty and personal-care company category-mix disclosures.
insights.quote: A new Women’s Wear Daily + BCG survey of 5,000 US beauty consumers reveals the industry is expanding beyond traditional beauty solutions.
insights.locator: Consumers Are Shaping a New Age of Optimization in Beauty

themes.theme: AI's Limits in Supply Chain Planning

insights.claim: BCG argues that in 2026 supply chain planning, AI technology itself is not what separates leading companies from laggards; the differentiator is how human planners apply advanced AI capabilities to evaluate tradeoffs, take action, and respond under pressure.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Counters the narrative that AI tooling alone drives supply-chain outperformance; implies investment payoff in enterprise AI depends more on organizational/process change management than on the underlying model or software purchase.
insights.quote: What separates leaders from laggards is not technology itself, but how planners apply advanced capabilities in evaluating tradeoffs, taking actions, and responding under pressure.
insights.locator: Supply Chain Planning 2026: Why AI Alone Isn’t Enough
